original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

actual_scope: Prove a directed cap for every A/B/restoration frame and fixed-G handoff chart refit of the PR2322 words, combined with fractional whole-helper packing on the same T74 stock.
scope_change_reason: New lender/early-restoration probes and source-alias count reductions did not improve the complete cost. The useful result is an exhaustive frame-optimization method and a cap on the newer fixed borrowed circuit, not a new helper inventory or the original construction acceptance gate.
bottleneck_link: Determines whether frame and owner optimization can materially lift the leading borrowed circuit before investing in another full replay.
stop_rule: Stop fixed-word frame search once complete finite-domain elimination and a directed packing dual establish a cap within 5.05e-9 of the observed primitive endpoint. Leave changes to gates, logical maps, endpoints and stock open.
evidence: EXPECTED.json: exhaustive min-sum elimination on complete transported subspace domains; maximum table 1953125 entries; both words, exact downward prices and 1163 packing inequalities force b<0.0016972. Rejection, independent brute-force, contraction and export controls.
author: Jeremy Diviney, with OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance with research, implementation, proof and verification. NumPy2.5.4 performs exact bounded int64 table operations. SciPy1.18.1/HiGHS nominated rational packing prices; OR-Tools and heuristic searches were discovery-only and are not proof dependencies.

open_questions.question: Can a changed scalar kernel, gate order or G map beat the cap?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those circuit choices are fixed by this result.
open_questions.first_step: Build an exact changed word and run the frame and whole-width gates before native/global admission.
open_questions.blocked_by: A fully correct arbitrary-input changed circuit.

open_questions.question: Can a changed parent inventory fit the helper widths more cheaply?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The bin stock is a hypothesis of the cap.
open_questions.first_step: Derive valid changed coverage and costs, then rerun the pattern dual.

open_questions.question: Can the elimination engine handle wider frame domains?

open_questions.first_step: Inspect the complete domain and separator sizes, then seek a lossless contraction.
open_questions.blocked_by: Memory growth of exact tables beyond the registered limit.
